samples.summary: The durable client's `WafflebaseDocStore` is never closed on unmount — an IndexedDB connection leaks per document opened
samples.evidence: `DurableYorkieProvider` creates the store in `useMemo(() => new WafflebaseDocStore({...}), [userId])` (line 135) and there is no `useEffect` returning `store.close()` anywhere between the memo and the `return` at line 209. Every other creator of this class releases it: `OfflineRuntime` calls `store.close()` in its effect cleanup (offline-runtime.tsx:195), `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout`/`retryPendingOfflineErase`/`purgeOfflineDocuments`/`purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments` all close in `finally`. Because `useMemo` is keyed on `userId`, navigating between documents in one session mounts/unmounts this provider repeatedly while `this.db` (set in `open()`'s `onsuccess`, wafflebase-doc-store.ts:482) is left open each time, so open IDB connections accumulate for the life of the tab. A held-open connection also participates in `onversionchange`/`deleteDatabase` blocking, which is the very reason `close()` exists ("so a `deleteDatabase` elsewhere is not blocked", wafflebase-doc-store.ts:494).
searchedFor: compared against OfflineRuntime, offline-erase.ts cleanup patterns

samples.summary: `DurableLossWatch` calls `doc.subscribe('local-changes-dropped'/'persist-disabled')` with no try/catch; an unsupported event name throws out of a passive effect and unmounts the whole editor subtree
samples.evidence: The effect guards only for `typeof doc.subscribe !== 'function'`, then calls `doc.subscribe('local-changes-dropped', ...)` and `doc.subscribe('persist-disabled', ...)` unguarded. Yorkie's `Document.subscribe` rejects unknown event names (it throws `YorkieError(ErrInvalidArgument, 'Unsupported event type')` for a first string argument that is neither a known keyword nor a `$`-path). The repo pins `@yorkie-js/sdk` 0.7.22 while `supportsClientKey()` gates only on the `@yorkie-js/react` pin (`__YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__`, yorkie-capabilities.ts:74-81) — so bumping react to 0.7.23 without the sdk activates this path against an sdk that may not know `persist-disabled`. The sibling component in this very change documents the consequence and defends against it: "a throw from a passive effect unmounts the tree: a missing avatar is a blemish, a blank editor is an outage" (collab-document-provider.tsx:83-85), and wraps its work in try/catch. This one does not. Secondary: if the second `subscribe` throws after the first succeeded, no cleanup is returned and the first subscription leaks.
searchedFor: attempted to read node_modules/@yorkie-js (not installed in checkout)

samples.summary: `collectStale` deletes other accounts' entries but asks its liveness question under the *sweeping* account's lock scope, so another account's open document can be purged out from under a live client with the loud-failure mark recorded in the wrong place
samples.evidence: `collectStale` deliberately sweeps entries "whoever wrote them" (line 1144-1151) and calls `this.isLive(docKey)` to spare open ones. But the only production supplier of `isOpenElsewhere` for this instance is `OfflineRuntime`, which passes `isOpenInAnyTab(docKey, { userId, whenUnknown: false })` (offline-runtime.tsx:74-75) — scoped to the signed-in user, and answering `false` when the runtime cannot tell. A second account's entry that is open in another tab therefore answers `not open`, is purged, and the compensating `this.evicted.add(docKey)` (line 1184) lands only in *this* tab's `evictedKeys` map (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:335-345, explicitly tab-local), so the other tab's next `appendChange` finds no header and takes the contract's silent "no base" success — every later edit going nowhere while its chip still reports the document saved. The 30-day staleness precondition plus `load()`'s best-effort `touch()` makes this narrow, but `touch()` swallows its own failures (line 569-571), so an entry can stay stale while attached.
searchedFor: read collectStale, isLive, evictedFor in wafflebase-doc-store.ts

samples.summary: `standDown` releases the Web Lock from inside a `setState` updater — a side effect in a function React requires to be pure and may invoke more than once or discard
samples.evidence: `setDecision((current) => { if (!current?.session) return current; current.session.release(); return { subject: current.subject }; })`. React may call an updater twice (StrictMode) or throw away the result of a render pass; releasing an app-wide Web Lock is an observable external side effect that must not be attached to that. Double invocation is currently harmless only because `acquireDurableSession`'s returned handle latches `released` (durable-session.ts), i.e. the safety comes from the other module rather than from this call site. If React discards the pass, the lock has been released while `decision` still reports the session.
searchedFor: read acquireDurableSession release guard in durable-session.ts

samples.summary: `watchForOfflineDisable`'s fallback `WafflebaseDocStore` is created but never closed
samples.evidence: `const current = store() ?? new WafflebaseDocStore({ userId: who });` — when the caller supplies no open store, a fresh store is constructed and `eraseOfflineData(current, who)` is fired and forgotten (`void ... .catch(...)`). Nothing calls `current.close()`, so the connection opened by that erase stays open for the life of the tab. Every other short-lived store in this module (`eraseOfflineDataOnLogout`, `retryPendingOfflineErase`, `purgeOfflineDocuments`, `purgeRevokedOfflineDocuments`) closes in a `finally`.

samples.summary: `lapse` falls through to `"another-tab"` for any non-durable reason the ternary chain does not enumerate, including "the election has not answered yet" and "no signed-in identity"
samples.evidence: The chain is `!supportsClientKey() ? unsupported : !permitted ? not-permitted : !offlineEnabled ? not-enabled : "another-tab"`. `decided` is `undefined` whenever the subject has not been latched yet or the component has stood down, and it is also `undefined`/non-durable when `person` is absent or the document key is `pdf-` prefixed (`isExcluded`, use-durable-document.ts:40). In all of those cases the tooltip asserts "This document is open in another tab, and that tab is the one saving it to this device" (sync-status-tooltip.ts LAPSE_REASONS), which is a specific factual claim the code has not established — the design requirement this implements is precisely that the tooltip "must name which case applies".
searchedFor: read the lapse ternary in collab-document-provider.tsx

Yorkie's `Document.subscribe` rejects unknown event names (it throws `YorkieError(ErrInvalidArgument, 'Unsupported event type')` for a first string argument that is neither a known keyword nor a `$`-path). searchedFor: attempted to read node_modules/@yorkie-js (not installed in checkout)

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described: durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:258-259 guards only `typeof doc.subscribe !== 'function' || typeof doc.getKey !== 'function'`, then calls doc.subscribe('local-changes-dropped', ...) at line 260 and doc.subscribe('persist-disabled', ...) at line 270 with no try/catch, and the cleanup at 273-276 is returned only if both succeed (so a throw from the second leaks the first). The sibling component in the same change documents the exact consequence and defends with a try/catch (collab-document-provider.tsx:80-92, 94-120), and DurableLossWatch is mounted unconditionally in every collaborative document (collab-document-provider.tsx:308). I could not refute on any named ground: (a) not-present fails — the code reads as quoted; (b) already-guarded fails — the only thing making the subscribe currently unreachable is the capability gate (yorkie-capabilities.ts:24,76-82 vs package.json:66,99 pinning react/sdk at 0.7.22, which makes useDurableDocument ineligible at use-durable-document.ts:127-132 and leaves the durable context absent so the effect returns at line 254), but that gate is explicitly designed to open on a single dependency bump (docs/tasks/active/20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md:37-41,242-246), so it postpones rather than removes reachability; (c) out-of-scope fails — an unhandled throw in a passive effect unmounting the editor subtree is squarely a correctness/crash concern. The one premise that would refute it — that Yorkie's Document.subscribe does not throw on an unrecognized event name — is unverifiable here: node_modules is absent and no SDK source or .d.ts is vendored (only src/vite-env.d.ts:5 declares anything yorkie-related). The repo's own docs say both events shipped by sdk 0.7.22 (docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:15-18,534,583), which weakens the version-skew scenario, but docs are not the SDK and say nothing about subscribe's behavior on unknown names. Unresolved uncertainty keeps the finding.

finding.summary: Recovery creates the offline copy with `createDocument({title, type})`, which omits the `workspaceId` the backend requires — so "Save a copy" always fails with a 400
finding.evidence: `recoverOfflineCopy` calls `createDocument({ title, type: source.type })` (line 210, and `{title, type:"note"}` at line 196). `packages/frontend/src/api/documents.ts:11-25` POSTs that payload verbatim to `${API}/documents`, which is `@Post('documents')` in `packages/backend/src/document/document.controller.ts:197` bound to `CreateDocumentInWorkspaceDto`. That DTO declares `@IsUUID() workspaceId: string` with **no** `@IsOptional()` (`packages/backend/src/document/document.dto.ts:84-85`), and `main.ts:73-79` installs a global `ValidationPipe({whitelist:true, forbidNonWhitelisted:true})`. A request with no `workspaceId` is therefore rejected with 400; `assertOk` throws, `recoverOfflineCopy` rejects, and `offline-runtime.tsx:285-288` swallows it into `toast.error('Could not recover those changes')`. The payoff path of the whole feature — handing back work the SDK could not reconcile — can never succeed. No test catches it: `offline-copy-recovery.test.ts` mocks `@/api/documents` `createDocument` wholesale, and `offline-runtime.test.tsx` mocks `recoverOfflineCopy`. (The other two no-workspace callers, `document-list.tsx:420` and `upload-queue.ts:234`, are conditional fallbacks; this new call site is unconditional.)

verdict.reason: The claimed code is not present. offline-copy-recovery.ts does not call `createDocument` at all — it imports `createWorkspaceDocument, fetchWorkspaces` from `@/api/workspaces` (line 4), and a grep for `createDocument` across packages/frontend/src/lib returns no matches. Both creation sites (lines 225-228 for notes, 242-245 for the general path) call `createWorkspaceDocument(await destinationWorkspace(source.workspaceId), { title, type })`. The reviewer's cited lines are also wrong: line 210 is `if (!rebuilt) {` and line 196 is a doc-comment opener. The workspaceId is supplied through the URL, not the body: api/workspaces.ts:359 POSTs to `${BASE}/${seg(workspaceId)}/documents`, which binds to document.controller.ts:115 `@Post('workspaces/:workspaceId/documents')` reading `@Param('workspaceId')` and binding the body to `CreateDocumentDto`, NOT the `CreateDocumentInWorkspaceDto` whose non-optional `@IsUUID() workspaceId` the whole finding depends on. So the global ValidationPipe never sees a missing workspaceId and no 400 occurs. Further, the file contains an explicit `destinationWorkspace()` helper (lines 174-184) that resolves the caller-supplied workspaceId and falls back to the user's first workspace via fetchWorkspaces(), throwing a named error only when the user has no workspace at all; its doc comment (lines 157-172) describes this exact failure mode in the past tense as already fixed. Both call sites route through that helper, so there is no bypassing path. The finding appears to have been written against a prior revision of the file.
